  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest

intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

# References

[1]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-opening
[2]: #refactor-split-loader-from-parser
[3]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-closing

# Closed: the last cycle's record

The last finished cycle's record, whole. A cycle's closing replaces this file's `## Closed` with
its own block from [zDOING.md](zDOING.md) and this file's references with that block's, so the
last record stays here until the next one is finished. Earlier cycles are in each landmark
commit's copy of the record.

## Closed

### feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and runs builds

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21, opened 2026-10-21) The last two work rungs of **feat: vc-x1 commit,
install, and run-dev**, deferred at its closing, run as their own cycle and widened at the opening
into three stages, dev, release, and the PATH, each with its command. The keys that cycle landed
as `[install] release`, `dev`, and `dev-bin` were read by nothing, and become `[build]`'s here.

#### Problem

Land's promotion is a hand-typed `cargo install --path .`, which checks nothing: it installs
whatever the working copy holds, pushed or not, at a suffixed version or a bare one, and it
replaces the PATH binary in the same step that builds the release, so the release is first run
when it is already the one consumers get. The `build.rs` guard that once refused a suffixed
version under the plain name is gone, and could never see the bookmark or the remote. The dev
binary lives off the PATH under `tmp/dev`, reached only by typing its path, and nothing says when
it is stale. The table that names the builds is read by nothing.

#### Solution

What was done. vc-x1 is not a build system: the config says what the steps are, and vc-x1 runs
them in order and checks their results, building before it runs or installs, reporting what it
is about to copy, refusing only a copy that would be wrong, and never letting the dev build
replace the release. Cargo decides what to rebuild.

| Command | What it does | When |
|---|---|---|
| `vc-x1 validate` | fmt, clippy, every test | every rung, before review |
| `vc-x1 validate --fast` | the unit tests only | while iterating |
| `vc-x1 build-dev` | the dev build, into `target/debug` | to build without running |
| `vc-x1 run-dev` | `build-dev`, then runs it | trying the change |
| `vc-x1 install-dev` | `build-dev`, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev` | trying the change elsewhere |
| `vc-x1 build` | the release, into `target/release` | at Land, or to try the release profile |
| `vc-x1 run` | `build`, then runs it, `run -- -V` the smoke check | before install |
| `vc-x1 install` | `build`, then reports it and copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` | at Land |

- `build` and `build-dev` run `[build] release` and `dev`, plain `cargo build --release --locked`
  and `cargo build --locked`, with the commit and state of the source in the commands'
  environment, so vc-x1's banner carries the commit wherever the binary is copied. A release
  checks it left `[build] release-bin`. Neither tracks staleness, which is cargo's: the stamp the
  build rung wrote went at the stamp rung.
- `install` and `install-dev` build first, report the binary from its `-V`, its version, its
  commit against `main` and `main@origin`, and its state, and refuse only a missing binary, a `-V`
  that will not run, or a missing directory. They copy `release-bin` into `[install] release-dir`
  and `dev-bin` into `dev-dir` with `dev-suffix`, `-dev` by default, appended, each as a temporary
  file renamed into place, safe over a running binary. `install-dev` refuses before the build a
  copy that would land on the release. `--dir` replaces the directory for one run, and
  `--dry-run` builds and reports and copies nothing.
- `[install] release` and `dev`, optional command lists, run in place of the built-in copy, their
  placeholders, `{build.release-bin}` and `{install.release-dir}` or the `dev` three, filled with
  the values resolved for the run. This workspace's lists write the copy out, so its config says
  what `install` does.
- `run` and `run-dev` build first, then run the binary in the current directory with the
  arguments untouched, after a warning when its `-V` is not the manifest's version, and exit with
  its code. An argument starting with `-` comes after `--`, as with `cargo run`. The words after
  either are completed by the binary it would run, asked in clap's completion mode and never
  built. All four build and run commands take `--dry-run`.
- `status` takes the write commands' four scopes, `w`, `a`, `b`, and `p`, through the one parser
  every `-s` uses.
- The schema's `[build]` holds `release`, `release-bin`, `dev`, and `dev-bin`, and `[install]`
  holds `release`, `release-dir`, `dev`, `dev-dir`, and `dev-suffix`, in `[build]`'s order. The
  model is regenerated, and this workspace's `.vc-config.md` carries the values. `[validate] full`
  no longer builds the dev binary.

#### Acceptance check

`build` leaves `target/release/vc-x1`, `run -- -V` prints the manifest's version, `build-dev` leaves
`target/debug/vc-x1` at the manifest's version, and `run-dev -- -V` prints it. `install --dry-run`
with nothing built builds the release, and on the cycle's bookmark reports the suffixed version, the
commit off `main`, and the dirty state. This cycle's own Land builds by the dev binary's `build`,
smoke-tests by its `run -- -V`, and installs by its `install`, the first install the command makes,
its report showing `main` and `main@origin`, clean, and a bare version.

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

its report showing `main` and `main@origin`, clean, and a bare version.

#### Deliberation

- Multi-step, five rungs, a trapezoid the default, the agent's proposal: opening, build stages the
  release, install deploys it, run and run-dev, closing.
  - Build first, since install reads its stamp and run reads its binary.
  - run and run-dev are one rung, sharing the binary's resolution, the pass-through, and the
    staleness check.
- Widened at the opening, wink's call (2026-10-21): a release staged under `tmp/rel` before it
  replaces anything on the PATH, `vc-x1 run` to run it, and a separate step onto the PATH. Folded
  in rather than filed, since it moves the guard, so building the release alone first would be
  rework. Retitled from "feat: vc-x1 install and run-dev" before the opening commit pushed, the
  bookmark renamed with it.
- The names, settled at the build rung (2026-10-21), wink's calls, in three steps:
  - `install --dev` became its own command, so each build has one, named with the `-dev` suffix
    as `run` and `run-dev` are: one rule, the suffix always meaning the dev build, and no dropped
    flag giving the other.
  - The private builds are `build` and `build-dev`, and `install` is the one step that touches
    the PATH, as `cargo install` means. They were `install`, `install-dev`, and `install-global`,
    where "install" for a build that reaches no PATH was the confusion. The table follows,
    `[build]` for the builds and `[install]` for the deploy.
  - `validate` checks the source and makes no build of either kind: `[validate] full` lost its
    dev build line, and `run-dev` builds first, as `cargo run` does. What runs is always the
    current code, after a fast validation too, which the line at the end of full could not
    promise, and the dev build has one definition, `[build] dev`. A dev binary run by its path
    can still be stale, which `run-dev` is the remedy for.
  - `validate` keeps its name, not `validate-dev`: it acts on the source, not a build, has no
    plain counterpart to tell apart, and the agent-files name it, so a rename is a proposal. A
    release validation, if one comes, is named beside it.
  - The cycle's title and its bookends keep the pushed name, "install stages, deploys, and runs
    builds", the opening being published, and the rungs not yet pushed take the new names.
- One build in `tmp/` during development, wink's practice (2026-10-21): the dev build lives in
  `tmp/dev` and the staged release in `tmp/rel` only from a deliberate `build` until it is
  installed, so no stale release sits beside the dev build to be run by mistake. wink removed the
  build rung's `tmp/rel` at the status rung, and Land's `build` stages a fresh one.
  - The builds moved to `target/` at the install rung, below, so a release build stays in
    `target/release` until `cargo clean`, and `run`'s version warning is what flags a stale one.
- Guidance on the nuances in one place, wink's ask at the status rung (2026-10-21): the closing
  rung's README update, close-out step 3, gathers one build in `tmp/` during development, the
  attached value forms `-sb` and `-s=b`, and the completion setup until the shim of **Shell
  completion installs itself and asks the binary typed** lands.
- The guard sits in the step consumers see, `install`, so `build` stages a release-profile build
  from a cycle's bookmark too, the check for a release-only failure mid-cycle. Superseded at the
  install rung, below: `install` reports and refuses only a wrong copy, and the guard is Land's.
- `install` copies rather than rebuilds: a second `cargo install` would deploy a fresh build, not

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21, opened 2026-10-23) Picked from `TODO.md` as **feat: vc-x1 land closes
a cycle and lands it**, retitled at the opening, wink's call, since the closing stays `commit
--closing` and the new command is `land`.

#### The Todo as picked

The close-out and Land are five commands typed in order, and each is a place to skip the sync,
move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. One command runs the sequence, with the review
between its commit and its pushes, filed at the first closing made by `commit --closing`.

- `vc-x1 land -s b [--from BOOKMARK] [--to BOOKMARK] [--title STR --body STR|@PATH]`, `--from`
  the cycle's bookmark, the line `@-` is on by default, and `--to` the trunk, `main` by default.
- The sequence, each step today's command:
  1. `sync -s b`: `--to` local equals its remote, or stop, since a moved trunk is the Land rule's
     stop.
  2. `commit -s w --closing --title --body`: the merge of `--to` and `--from`'s tip.
  3. The review: `jj show @-`, and the command waits for the go, or `--yes` under a waiver.
  4. `move-bookmark -s w --bookmark <to> --target @-`: the fast-forward, no `--allow-backwards`.
  5. `push -s b <to>`: the agent half commits the journal as the partner, the work half publishes
     `--to`. The closing never reaches `--from`'s remote, so the two pushes of the by-hand Land
     are one.
  6. `build`, a `run -- -V` smoke check, and `install`, since they stage and deploy what `--to`
     now carries, the commands **feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and runs builds** made.
  7. Delete `--from` locally and remotely, once `vc-x1` owns bookmark deletion. Until then it
     prints the two `jj` lines.
- Interactive: with no `--title` and `--body` it opens `$EDITOR`, as `jj describe` and `git gui`
  do, on a buffer pre-filled with the bookend's text, the title from the In Progress block's and
  the body `Closes the cycle "<title>". Its record is the Closed block in zCLOSED.md.`, so the
  common case is save and quit. This is the editor path `commit` left out until asked for.
- `--dry-run` prints the seven steps with what each would do, and does nothing.
- Not `commit -s b`: the journal of the command's own review is what the push commits as the
  partner.
- Wants bookmark deletion in `vc-x1` for step 7, which may land as its own cycle before this one.
  Step 6's commands are there.
- A single-step cycle skips steps 2 and 3: its one commit is on `main` already, titled with the
  bare cycle title, so there is no ladder to merge and `commit --closing` refuses one, by design
  and its test `closing_with_no_ladder_is_refused`. Its Land is the sync, the fast-forward of
  `--to` to the commit, the push, the install, and the deletion, so the command tells the two
  shapes apart, by the commits between `--to` and `--from`'s tip, one for a single-step cycle and
  at least two for a ladder, its opening and a rung, and says which it ran. (wink + agent,
  2026-10-22)

##### Two commands, and their undos

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21) The sequence above splits in two at the review, the names placeholders
until the opening:

- `vc-x1 close-out-commit --bookmark <x>`, `<x>` the current bookmark by default: the closing
  merge, made locally, and reviewed like any rung's commit, by `jj show @-` or gitk.
- `vc-x1 land-it --from <x> --to <y>`, `<x>` the current bookmark and `<y>` `main` by default:
  what follows the go, sync, the fast-forward, the push, the install, and the bookmark's deletion.
- So the review leaves the command. The agent's shell cannot answer a prompt, so a wait inside
  `land` would need `--yes` on every agent run, and the editor path goes with it. The split also
  matches v0.3.1's local commit pair before every push.
- Bookmark deletion is a rung of this cycle, a subcommand or a flag on `move-bookmark`, rather
  than a cycle of its own, since nothing else waits on it.

Defaults invite mistakes, and the two undos differ:

- **close-out-commit's undo is local and wanted now.** The closing never reaches the bookmark's
  remote, so undoing it rewrites nothing anyone has seen. jj's own undo is one repo's operation
  log and the command writes two, so the undo's worth is doing both sides together. The agent side
  is uncommitted, its content moved back into `@`, never restored to an earlier operation, which
  would roll back the session transcript and drop the lines written since. We think the operation
  restore is safe on the work side alone.
- **land-it is guarded rather than undone.** Its push moves `main@origin`, and undoing that is a
  force-move of the trunk backward, so a revert commit is the undo and moving `main` back sits
  behind an explicit flag. The deletion is undone by recreating the bookmark at the commit
  land-it printed, and the install by reinstalling from the previous `main`, which it also prints.
  A run stopped partway wants a resume, or an undo of the local steps not yet pushed, more than a
  finished land wants an undo.
- **Current** is the nearest bookmark on `@-`'s ancestry that is not the trunk. With `@` on `main`
  and no topic bookmark it would resolve to `main`, so both commands refuse that, and land-it
  refuses `--from` equal to `--to`.
- **land-it lands only a close-out**: the commit it lands must be a merge whose parents are `--to`
  and `--from`'s tip, the shape close-out-commit makes, so a cycle not closed out, or closed onto
  the wrong trunk, is refused.
- Both print what their defaults resolved to before acting, and `--dry-run` prints only that.
  land-it stops before its push with the plan printed, the last point where its undo is local.
- The lean: close-out-commit's undo in this cycle, as a flag or a sibling command. land-it's true
  undo, after the push, waits until a real mistake asks for it.

  rung, and pushed on its own go, and `land` is everything after the Land go.
  - The agent's shell cannot answer a prompt, so a review inside one command needs `--yes` on
    every agent run, and the editor path goes with it.
- The closing stays `commit --closing`, wink's call at the opening (2026-10-23), not a new
  `close-out-commit`: it exists, its tests exist, and `--closing` matches the bookend's
  " closing". The second command is `land`, the protocol's own word, and the cycle is retitled to
  match.
- `commit --closing` handles every cycle shape, each tested, wink's call at the opening
  (2026-10-23): no ladder, a single-step cycle; a ladder of one rung, the opening alone, which
  [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape) says still closes as a ladder; two rungs, the only size
  tested today; and three or more.
  - The Todo's single-step line is mistaken: a single-step cycle's one commit is on its bookmark,
    not on `main`, since `main` advances only at Land. So the commit is made above `main`, and
    today's `has_ladder` would call that a ladder, which the closing rung settles.
  - The provisional single-step behavior: `--closing` with the work `@-` on `main` makes the one
    commit plain, under the bare cycle title, and says it is a single-step cycle's, rather than
    being refused. We think the title is the way to tell a one-rung ladder from a single-step
    commit already pushed, the opening's ending " opening", since both are one commit above
    `main`.

  rung. `land`'s undo, after its push, waits for a real mistake.

#### Problem

Closing a cycle and landing it are five commands typed in order, sync, the closing commit, the
fast-forward, the push, and the install, then two `jj` lines to delete the bookmark, each a place to
skip the sync, move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. `commit --closing` is tested on a
ladder of two rungs only and refuses a single-step cycle, and a closing made by mistake is undone by
hand in two repos.

Provisional. `commit --closing` closes every cycle shape and can be taken back in both repos at
once, `vc-x1` deletes a bookmark locally and remotely, and `vc-x1 land` runs what follows the Land
go: the sync, the fast-forward of the trunk to the closing, the push, the build, the smoke check, the
install, and the bookmark's deletion, printing what its defaults resolved to first and what undoes
each step after.

two, and of three, a test of the closing's undo restoring both repos, and `land` tests landing a
single-step cycle and a ladder on fixtures and refusing a commit that is neither shape. This
cycle's own Land is run by the dev build's `vc-x1 land`, its report showing `main` and
`main@origin` at the closing, the bookmark gone locally and remotely, and the installed `vc-x1 -V`
a bare 0.85.8.

  undo, after the push, waits until a real mistake asks for it.

  rung, and pushed on its own go, and `land` is everything after the Land go.

  match.

    `main`.

  rung. `land`'s undo, after its push, waits for a real mistake.

fast-forward, the push, and the install, then two `jj` lines to delete the bookmark, each a place to
skip the sync, move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. `commit --closing` is tested on a
ladder of two rungs only and refuses a single-step cycle, and a closing made by mistake is undone by
hand in two repos.

once, `vc-x1` deletes a bookmark locally and remotely, and `vc-x1 land` runs what follows the Land
go: the sync, the fast-forward of the trunk to the closing, the push, the build, the smoke check, the
install, and the bookmark's deletion, printing what its defaults resolved to first and what undoes

## In Progress

### feat: vc-x1 closing and land

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21, opened 2026-10-23) Picked from `TODO.md` as **feat: vc-x1 land closes
a cycle and lands it**, retitled at the opening, wink's call, since the closing stays `commit
--closing` and the new command is `land`.

#### The Todo as picked

The close-out and Land are five commands typed in order, and each is a place to skip the sync,
move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. One command runs the sequence, with the review
between its commit and its pushes, filed at the first closing made by `commit --closing`.

- `vc-x1 land -s b [--from BOOKMARK] [--to BOOKMARK] [--title STR --body STR|@PATH]`, `--from`
  the cycle's bookmark, the line `@-` is on by default, and `--to` the trunk, `main` by default.
- The sequence, each step today's command:
  1. `sync -s b`: `--to` local equals its remote, or stop, since a moved trunk is the Land rule's
     stop.
  2. `commit -s w --closing --title --body`: the merge of `--to` and `--from`'s tip.
  3. The review: `jj show @-`, and the command waits for the go, or `--yes` under a waiver.
  4. `move-bookmark -s w --bookmark <to> --target @-`: the fast-forward, no `--allow-backwards`.
  5. `push -s b <to>`: the agent half commits the journal as the partner, the work half publishes
     `--to`. The closing never reaches `--from`'s remote, so the two pushes of the by-hand Land
     are one.
  6. `build`, a `run -- -V` smoke check, and `install`, since they stage and deploy what `--to`
     now carries, the commands **feat: vc-x1 install stages, deploys, and runs builds** made.
  7. Delete `--from` locally and remotely, once `vc-x1` owns bookmark deletion. Until then it
     prints the two `jj` lines.
- Interactive: with no `--title` and `--body` it opens `$EDITOR`, as `jj describe` and `git gui`
  do, on a buffer pre-filled with the bookend's text, the title from the In Progress block's and
  the body `Closes the cycle "<title>". Its record is the Closed block in zCLOSED.md.`, so the
  common case is save and quit. This is the editor path `commit` left out until asked for.
- `--dry-run` prints the seven steps with what each would do, and does nothing.
- Not `commit -s b`: the journal of the command's own review is what the push commits as the
  partner.
- Wants bookmark deletion in `vc-x1` for step 7, which may land as its own cycle before this one.
  Step 6's commands are there.
- A single-step cycle skips steps 2 and 3: its one commit is on `main` already, titled with the
  bare cycle title, so there is no ladder to merge and `commit --closing` refuses one, by design
  and its test `closing_with_no_ladder_is_refused`. Its Land is the sync, the fast-forward of
  `--to` to the commit, the push, the install, and the deletion, so the command tells the two
  shapes apart, by the commits between `--to` and `--from`'s tip, one for a single-step cycle and
  at least two for a ladder, its opening and a rung, and says which it ran. (wink + agent,
  2026-10-22)

##### Two commands, and their undos

(wink + agent, 2026-10-21) The sequence above splits in two at the review, the names placeholders
until the opening:

- `vc-x1 close-out-commit --bookmark <x>`, `<x>` the current bookmark by default: the closing
  merge, made locally, and reviewed like any rung's commit, by `jj show @-` or gitk.
- `vc-x1 land-it --from <x> --to <y>`, `<x>` the current bookmark and `<y>` `main` by default:
  what follows the go, sync, the fast-forward, the push, the install, and the bookmark's deletion.
- So the review leaves the command. The agent's shell cannot answer a prompt, so a wait inside
  `land` would need `--yes` on every agent run, and the editor path goes with it. The split also
  matches v0.3.1's local commit pair before every push.
- Bookmark deletion is a rung of this cycle, a subcommand or a flag on `move-bookmark`, rather
  than a cycle of its own, since nothing else waits on it.

Defaults invite mistakes, and the two undos differ:

- **close-out-commit's undo is local and wanted now.** The closing never reaches the bookmark's
  remote, so undoing it rewrites nothing anyone has seen. jj's own undo is one repo's operation
  log and the command writes two, so the undo's worth is doing both sides together. The agent side
  is uncommitted, its content moved back into `@`, never restored to an earlier operation, which
  would roll back the session transcript and drop the lines written since. We think the operation
  restore is safe on the work side alone.
- **land-it is guarded rather than undone.** Its push moves `main@origin`, and undoing that is a
  force-move of the trunk backward, so a revert commit is the undo and moving `main` back sits
  behind an explicit flag. The deletion is undone by recreating the bookmark at the commit
  land-it printed, and the install by reinstalling from the previous `main`, which it also prints.
  A run stopped partway wants a resume, or an undo of the local steps not yet pushed, more than a
  finished land wants an undo.
- **Current** is the nearest bookmark on `@-`'s ancestry that is not the trunk. With `@` on `main`
  and no topic bookmark it would resolve to `main`, so both commands refuse that, and land-it
  refuses `--from` equal to `--to`.
- **land-it lands only a close-out**: the commit it lands must be a merge whose parents are `--to`
  and `--from`'s tip, the shape close-out-commit makes, so a cycle not closed out, or closed onto
  the wrong trunk, is refused.
- Both print what their defaults resolved to before acting, and `--dry-run` prints only that.
  land-it stops before its push with the plan printed, the last point where its undo is local.
- The lean: close-out-commit's undo in this cycle, as a flag or a sibling command. land-it's true
  undo, after the push, waits until a real mistake asks for it.

#### Deliberation

- Two commands, split at the review, the Todo's own lean: the closing is made, reviewed like any
  rung, and pushed on its own go, and `land` is everything after the Land go.
  - The agent's shell cannot answer a prompt, so a review inside one command needs `--yes` on
    every agent run, and the editor path goes with it.
- The closing stays `commit --closing`, wink's call at the opening (2026-10-23), not a new
  `close-out-commit`: it exists, its tests exist, and `--closing` matches the bookend's
  " closing". The second command is `land`, the protocol's own word, and the cycle is retitled to
  match.
- `commit --closing` handles every cycle shape, each tested, wink's call at the opening
  (2026-10-23): no ladder, a single-step cycle; a ladder of one rung, the opening alone, which
  [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape) says still closes as a ladder; two rungs, the only size
  tested today; and three or more.
  - The Todo's single-step line is mistaken: a single-step cycle's one commit is on its bookmark,
    not on `main`, since `main` advances only at Land. So the commit is made above `main`, and
    today's `has_ladder` would call that a ladder, which the closing rung settles.
  - The provisional single-step behavior: `--closing` with the work `@-` on `main` makes the one
    commit plain, under the bare cycle title, and says it is a single-step cycle's, rather than
    being refused. We think the title is the way to tell a one-rung ladder from a single-step
    commit already pushed, the opening's ending " opening", since both are one commit above
    `main`.
- The closing's undo is in this cycle, the Todo's lean, a flag or a sibling command settled at its
  rung. `land`'s undo, after its push, waits for a real mistake.
- Bookmark deletion is a rung of this cycle, not its own cycle, since only `land` waits on it.
- `land` lands two shapes and refuses anything else: a closing merge whose parents are `--to` and
  the ladder's tip, or a single-step cycle's one commit whose parent is `--to`.
- Multi-step, five rungs between the bookends' sides, the agent's proposal: the closing's shapes
  first since `land` reads them, then its undo, then deletion, then `land`, which uses all three.

#### Problem

Closing a cycle and landing it are five commands typed in order, sync, the closing commit, the
fast-forward, the push, and the install, then two `jj` lines to delete the bookmark, each a place to
skip the sync, move the wrong bookmark, or push before the review. `commit --closing` is tested on a
ladder of two rungs only and refuses a single-step cycle, and a closing made by mistake is undone by
hand in two repos.

#### Solution

Provisional. `commit --closing` closes every cycle shape and can be taken back in both repos at
once, `vc-x1` deletes a bookmark locally and remotely, and `vc-x1 land` runs what follows the Land
go: the sync, the fast-forward of the trunk to the closing, the push, the build, the smoke check, the
install, and the bookmark's deletion, printing what its defaults resolved to first and what undoes
each step after.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with `commit --closing` tests for a single-step cycle, a ladder of one rung, of
two, and of three, a test of the closing's undo restoring both repos, and `land` tests landing a
single-step cycle and a ladder on fixtures and refusing a commit that is neither shape. This
cycle's own Land is run by the dev build's `vc-x1 land`, its report showing `main` and
`main@origin` at the closing, the bookmark gone locally and remotely, and the installed `vc-x1 -V`
a bare 0.85.8.

#### Ladder

- [feat: vc-x1 closing and land opening][1] (current)
- [feat: commit --closing closes every cycle shape][2]
- [feat: the closing can be taken back][3]
- [feat: vc-x1 deletes a bookmark][4]
- [feat: vc-x1 land lands a closed cycle][5]
- [feat: vc-x1 closing and land closing][6]

##### feat: vc-x1 closing and land opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, move the Todo entry into this block,
and bump the version-of-record.

##### feat: commit --closing closes every cycle shape

`commit --closing` is tested on a ladder of two rungs and refuses a single-step cycle, so it makes
the single-step commit and closes a ladder of one, two, and three or more rungs, each tested.

##### feat: the closing can be taken back

A closing made by mistake is undone by hand in two repos, so one invocation takes it back, the
work side by its operation and the agent side's content moved back into `@`.

##### feat: vc-x1 deletes a bookmark

Deleting a cycle's bookmark is two `jj` lines, so `vc-x1` deletes one locally and remotely, a
subcommand or a `move-bookmark` flag settled at the rung.

##### feat: vc-x1 land lands a closed cycle

Land is typed by hand, so `vc-x1 land` checks the shape, syncs, fast-forwards the trunk, pushes,
builds, smoke-checks, installs, and deletes the bookmark, for both cycle shapes.

##### feat: vc-x1 closing and land closing

Closing out the cycle.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

content.content:
vc-x1 0.85.7+10910617960a

Publish a rung's pair: the work commit on its bookmark and the
agent commit on `main`. Push carries no description and writes
none, so what was reviewed is what goes out.

`commit` makes the pair, both commits now (-s b) or the work
half with its trailer naming the agent @ (-s w). Push refuses a
work @ that is not empty, unsquashed work being a fix to fold
or the next rung, and a work @- with no `ochid:` trailer, which
is not a pair's commit.

The halves are independent, each trailer being fixed before
push runs, so -s b is -s a then -s w, the order the pair is
completed in:
  - agent  complete the partner by the state found: fold the
           journal into a committed one, or commit it as the
           partner when pending or the agent repo changed;
           then squash-push main
  - work   restamp the unpublished work commit if its trailer
           does not name the partner, then set and push
           <bookmark>

-s is required: `b` both halves, `a` the agent half, `w` the work
half, `p` a plain repo's @- on its bookmark. -R is optional and
says where. The bookmark is the line's unless named as a check.

Rerunning is always safe: a half whose work is done finds nothing
to do. A half that fails before its own push restores the repo it
touched via `jj op restore`.

Usage: vc-x1 push [OPTIONS] --scope <SCOPE> [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Work-repo bookmark to advance, a check against the line `@-` is on
          [default: the bookmark of that line]

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
